about: Sourced story details for the 1700 era (docs/PEOPLE-1700.md). Items carry confidence (documented | derived | inferred | later-recorded | INVENTED), an uncertain flag, source ids (A.. pilots, B.. hamlet, C.. war, D.. storms) and a useFor note. INVENTED items are suggestions, not history; later-recorded beliefs are not proof for 1700. No person, station or boat is named unless a source names it. Read 2026-11-06.

items.text: Lysekil pilot station set up 'early 1700s'; 4 pilots + 2 apprentices 1729; 4 pilots + 4 lotsdrängar 1744.
items.useFor: The only documented station in the game's box.

items.text: No source names a pilot station at Grundsund, Skaftö, Fiskebäckskil or Härmanö; Grundsund is not on the 1940 list of pilot places.
items.useFor: Torhild's family piloting from Grundsund is plausible but informal.

items.text: 1696 regulation (19 Sept): exam and oath for pilots and lotsdrängar, Swedish subjects only, penalties up to nine gatlopp or death; each pilot takes an apprentice.
items.useFor: Torhild's fear of a mistake; her father's rules.

items.text: West and south coast were regulated only at the larger harbours in the late 1600s; Western/Northern districts only from 1724.
items.useFor: Why Grundsund piloting is informal.

items.text: Pilots were paid per ship (lotspenning); lotshemman holders also farmed and fished, tax-exempt; pilotage often inherited.
items.useFor: Poor in quiet seasons; fishing and croft alongside. Not dated to 1700.

items.text: Käringön pilot Olof Eriksson Ström (b. c.1640) piloted Norwegian ships around 1710 with Peder Wessel aboard.
items.useFor: Norwegian sympathies lingered from before 1658; guess is the source's own.

items.text: Lysekil pilot supervisor Peter Nilsson (appointed 1700) quit in 1714, saying Norwegians ruined him in 1711.
items.useFor: War pressure on pilots; thin (one case).

items.text: Period definition (1736): 'Et Skepp är på lägervall, när vinden ligger mitt åt landet...' (lee shore).
items.useFor: Dialogue flavour; a seamanship definition, not a pilot's saying.

items.text: Nearest light: Nidingen (Halland), coal fire from the 1620s-40s; none in Bohuslän before Carlsten 1782.
items.useFor: Why Torhild has only dreamed of lights.

items.text: No documented signals to call a pilot, vårdkase sites, named leading marks, or pilot daughters/wives c.1700.
items.useFor: Gaps; do not present these as facts.

items.text: Torhild reads the fairway by transit marks and rock names learned on the water; helps with fishing, croft and the boat; fears a pilot's mistake.
items.useFor: Her teaching tasks in the lab (line up the cairn and the notch). Specific marks invented.

items.text: Strandsittare rented the ground under their house (grundlega); the house counted as movable property.
items.useFor: A hamlet can be moved. The legal wording comes from an 1899 report.

items.text: Gullholmen: 24 strandsittare 1610, about 39 households 1645, 20 fishing families end of the 1600s.
items.useFor: Last figure is secondhand (1840s author).

items.text: Many strandsittar places vanished around the early 1700s (Härmanösund, Vallerö, Lyreleje): tax, lost trade, wartime plunder.
items.useFor: Abandoned hamlet with a stone ring and hearth to find.

items.text: Gullholmen harbour wreck called 'Tordenskiold's ship' is tree-ring dated: latest ring 1717 with no sapwood, so probably felled 1727-1827 (no earlier than the 1720s); the museum rejects the Tordenskiold link; one oak treenail shows fire damage, so the ship may have burned (Bohusläns museum rapport 2012:39, via data/island-lore.json).
items.useFor: A legend a villager insists on.

items.text: Documented Bohuslän fishing boat c.1700-1850: tosejlare (hook-and-line, to Skagen for plaice); eka with sprit sail is plausible but only 20th-century examples survive.
items.useFor: The player's tarred eka is a design choice (BOAT-BRIEF).

items.text: Kalm 1742: fishermen and pilots' weather signs (mist coiling round the hills = storm from S/SW/W; roaring sea after calm shows the wind's quarter; two cloud banks 'weigh against each other').
items.useFor: Wording for fog and weather warnings. OCR unproofread; 1742, not 1700.

items.text: Gast, fej, departure taboos, fläckkniv, anchor-chain blessing, rooster over a drowned body.
items.useFor: Texture for the grandmother's stories; flag as 20th-century informants.

items.text: Havsrå: a Bohuslän version from a man born 1859 (night or before storms, glowing, lures men to the skerries). Swedish Wikipedia treats sjörå as a lake spirit; draug is Norwegian; irrbloss/lyktgubbe are land lights.
items.useFor: A phantom light at sea would be invented.

items.text: Timber was scarce (heavy cutting 1500s-1600s; Kalm 1742 'bald hills').
items.useFor: Boat and fuel cost.

items.text: c.1700 houses, food, clothing, gear, women's and children's work, taboo words, wreck-law attitudes: not found.
items.useFor: Gaps; ask a museum before inventing.

items.text: Dynekilen, 8 July 1716 (new style): Tordenskiold's force got hold of a Swedish sailor who had earlier piloted the Swedish transports into the ~100 m wide fjord. Name not given.
items.useFor: Torhild's father/uncle as a pilot who fears being taken. The character is invented.

items.text: Koster fishermen reportedly told the Danes about the fleet and the officers' wedding at Dyne farm.
items.useFor: Divided loyalties after 1658. One secondary page; cited work not seen.

items.text: Olof Strömstierna (born Knape, 1664-1730), commander at Dynekilen, led the first Bohuslän båtsman company from 1704; sv.wikipedia says born on Käringön.
items.useFor: Local-pride hook. en.wikipedia disagrees on birthplace and father.

items.text: Marstrand 1719: five frigates scuttled by the Swedes on 11-12 July (old style); Colonel Danckwardt executed 16 Sept 1719.
items.useFor: Masts in the harbour. Salvage by locals is invented.

items.text: Lars Gathenhielm (1689-1718) operated from Gothenburg, not Marstrand.
items.useFor: Corrects the design/brief notes.

items.text: Strömstad 1717: Tordenskiold's attack failed; 1718: Karl XII's base with barracks and a galley road to the Idefjord; Karl XII died 11 Dec 1718.
items.useFor: Rumour of the king's death along the coast.

items.text: Danish naval ensign was swallow-tailed (regulated 1625); ship names Hjælperen, Hvide Ørn (ex-Swedish Hvita Örn), Vindhunden. Exact flags on the 1716-19 ships not verified.
items.useFor: Echo with Svalan. Do not assert a specific flag design.

items.text: 1714: the privateer Olbing Galley fought Tordenskiold's Løvendals Galej off Lindesnes; the captains exchanged toasts.
items.useFor: A courteous-enemy scene. Norwegian coast, 1714.

items.text: Billeting, requisition, vårdkase watches, refugees, forced pilotage by Tordenskiold, raids tied to Lysekil/Skaftö/Fiskebäckskil: not found. The 1710 plague is documented for Skåne, Stockholm and Karlshamn only.
items.useFor: Gaps.

items.text: The Great Storm of 1703 (26-27 Nov old style) hit England, the Channel, the Low Countries and northern Germany; KNMI says Scandinavia was under high pressure. North Sea only.
items.useFor: Do not claim it hit Bohuslän.

items.text: One Wikipedia sentence: HMS Association was blown from Harwich to Gothenburg.
items.useFor: Hook only: a storm that drives a ship across to this coast.

items.text: Christmas Flood 1717: damage on the Dutch, German and Danish/Schleswig North Sea coasts; nothing supports Bohuslän.
items.useFor: Do not use as a Bohuslän storm.

items.text: Cold years: famine 1695-97 (worst in Finland and Norrland), Great Frost 1709; no Bohuslän detail.
items.useFor: Background only.

items.text: No named great storm on the Bohuslän coast in 1650-1725 found; no shipwreck lists, church-record notes or ice records.
items.useFor: Gap.

items.text: Game storm: a local gale, optionally echoing late November 1703 (old style) as a mood; weather signs before it from Kalm 1742.
items.useFor: Do not name it a historical storm.

items.text: Lysekil around 1703 is not a hamlet: a fishing place older than the herring period 1566-1587 with its own church and priest, 82 adults in 1645 (half strandsittare), part of Lysekil parish from 1700, a pilot station set up early in the 1700s (4 pilots in 1729), and a town only from 1 April 1903.
items.useFor: Torhild's home: a small working fishing place with a church and a pilot station, not a bare hamlet and not yet a town.
